Basic Concepts in Government.text: Power, in political science, is best defined as
options: the legal right to rule, granted by a constitution
the ability to influence or control the behaviour of others, with or without their consent
the moral acceptance of a ruler by the people
the supreme, unquestionable control a state has over its territory
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: the ability to influence or control the behaviour of others, with or without their consent

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Authority differs from power mainly in that authority is
options: power that is exercised without any legal or moral backing
power that is recognized as legitimate and rightfully exercised
identical to power in every meaningful respect
exercised only by military rulers
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: power that is recognized as legitimate and rightfully exercised

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Legitimacy refers to
options: the physical capacity of a government to enforce its will by force alone
the general acceptance of a government’s right to rule by the people it governs
a government’s international recognition alone, with no reference to its own citizens
a quality possessed only by democratically elected governments
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: the general acceptance of a government’s right to rule by the people it governs

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Sovereignty is best described as
options: the supreme and final authority of a state over its territory and people, both internally and externally
the ability of a state to trade with other nations
a quality that only applies to the executive arm of government
the same concept as legitimacy
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: the supreme and final authority of a state over its territory and people, both internally and externally

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Internal sovereignty refers to a state’s
options: supreme authority within its own territory, over all persons and institutions
recognition by other independent states
membership of international organizations
control of its foreign embassies alone
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: supreme authority within its own territory, over all persons and institutions

Basic Concepts in Government.text: External sovereignty refers to a state’s
options: supreme authority over its own citizens alone
independence from external control, and its recognition as an equal among other sovereign states
power to tax its citizens
control over its judiciary alone
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: independence from external control, and its recognition as an equal among other sovereign states

Basic Concepts in Government.text: A society, in political terms, refers to
options: a group of people who share a common government and defined territory
a group of people living together, sharing common customs, traditions, and organized social relationships, not necessarily under a single government
a term identical in every respect to “state”
a purely economic unit with no cultural dimension
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: a group of people living together, sharing common customs, traditions, and organized social relationships, not necessarily under a single government

Basic Concepts in Government.text: A state is generally defined as
options: a group of people with shared customs but no defined territory
a political and legal entity possessing a defined territory, population, government, and sovereignty
a term identical in every respect to “nation”
any organization that collects taxes
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: a political and legal entity possessing a defined territory, population, government, and sovereignty

Basic Concepts in Government.text: A nation refers to
options: a group of people bound together by a defined territory and government alone
a group of people who share a common identity, often based on shared language, culture, history, or ethnicity, regardless of political boundaries
a term identical in every respect to “state”
only a group recognized by the United Nations
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: a group of people who share a common identity, often based on shared language, culture, history, or ethnicity, regardless of political boundaries

Basic Concepts in Government.text: A nation-state refers to
options: a state whose population is composed of several distinct nations with no shared identity
a state in which the population largely shares a common national identity, coinciding with the boundaries of the state
a purely economic association of independent nations
a term with no meaningful political application
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: a state in which the population largely shares a common national identity, coinciding with the boundaries of the state

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Political processes generally refer to
options: the fixed, unchanging structure of a country’s constitution
the ongoing activities, interactions, and procedures through which political decisions are made and power is exercised
only the activities of the judiciary
a concept limited strictly to elections
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: the ongoing activities, interactions, and procedures through which political decisions are made and power is exercised

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Political socialization refers to the process by which
options: individuals acquire their political values, beliefs, and attitudes, typically through family, school, media, and other social institutions
political parties are formed
a government transitions from one regime to another
citizens are stripped of their voting rights
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: individuals acquire their political values, beliefs, and attitudes, typically through family, school, media, and other social institutions

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Political participation refers to
options: the activities of citizens aimed at influencing government decisions, policies, or the selection of political leaders
the study of a country’s constitution alone
a concept limited strictly to holding public office
a purely academic exercise with no practical political effect
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: the activities of citizens aimed at influencing government decisions, policies, or the selection of political leaders

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Political culture refers to
options: the artistic traditions of a given ethnic group
the shared pattern of political attitudes, values, beliefs, and orientations held by members of a given political community
the formal legal structure of a country’s government
a term synonymous with political party membership
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: the shared pattern of political attitudes, values, beliefs, and orientations held by members of a given political community

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes power from authority?
options: Power always requires legitimacy, while authority does not
Power is the raw capacity to compel behaviour, whereas authority is power exercised with a recognized right to do so
They are identical concepts, used interchangeably in political science
Authority can never be backed by power
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: Power is the raw capacity to compel behaviour, whereas authority is power exercised with a recognized right to do so

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a government may possess power but lack legitimacy?
options: A government can enforce compliance through coercion or force, without necessarily being accepted by the populace as having a rightful claim to rule
Power and legitimacy are always identical, so this situation could never arise
A government automatically loses all power the moment it loses legitimacy
Legitimacy is granted only by international bodies, never by a state’s own citizens
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: A government can enforce compliance through coercion or force, without necessarily being accepted by the populace as having a rightful claim to rule

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains the relationship between sovereignty and statehood?
options: Sovereignty is irrelevant to whether an entity qualifies as a state
Sovereignty, both internal and external, is generally considered a defining characteristic that distinguishes a fully independent state from a mere territory or colony
A colony automatically possesses full sovereignty
Only member states of the United Nations can be considered sovereign
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: Sovereignty, both internal and external, is generally considered a defining characteristic that distinguishes a fully independent state from a mere territory or colony

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a nation from a state?
options: A nation is defined strictly by legal and territorial boundaries, while a state is defined by shared culture
A nation is based primarily on shared identity (such as culture, language, or history), while a state is a political and legal entity with defined territory and government
The two terms are entirely interchangeable, with no meaningful distinction
A nation must always possess its own government, while a state need not
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: A nation is based primarily on shared identity (such as culture, language, or history), while a state is a political and legal entity with defined territory and government

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Which of the following correctly illustrates the concept of a nation-state?
options: A state comprising several ethnic groups with no shared sense of common identity
A state such as Japan, where the population largely shares a common national identity coinciding with the state’s boundaries
A purely economic union of otherwise unrelated countries
Any territory administered by a colonial power
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: A state such as Japan, where the population largely shares a common national identity coinciding with the state’s boundaries

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains the role of political socialization in shaping a country’s political culture?
options: Political socialization has no bearing on political culture
Through political socialization, individuals absorb the shared values, beliefs, and attitudes that collectively constitute a society’s political culture
Political culture is fixed at a nation’s founding and cannot be influenced by socialization
Political socialization occurs only among elected officials
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: Through political socialization, individuals absorb the shared values, beliefs, and attitudes that collectively constitute a society’s political culture

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why political participation is considered essential to democratic governance?
options: It has no meaningful effect on government decision-making
It allows citizens to influence government policies and hold leaders accountable, reinforcing the legitimacy of democratic institutions
It applies only to citizens who hold public office
It is relevant only in authoritarian systems
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: It allows citizens to influence government policies and hold leaders accountable, reinforcing the legitimacy of democratic institutions

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Which of the following best illustrates the exercise of legitimate authority, as opposed to mere power?
options: An armed group seizing control of a town through force alone
An elected president enforcing laws passed by a duly constituted legislature
A group of citizens ignoring court rulings they personally disagree with
A foreign army occupying a territory without local consent
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: An elected president enforcing laws passed by a duly constituted legislature

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why sovereignty is considered a foundational concept in the study of international relations?
options: Sovereignty determines a state’s right to govern itself free from external interference, forming the basis of state equality and non-intervention in international law
Sovereignty is relevant only to domestic law, with no bearing on international relations
Sovereign states are exempt from any international obligations whatsoever
Sovereignty has been entirely abolished under modern international law
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: Sovereignty determines a state’s right to govern itself free from external interference, forming the basis of state equality and non-intervention in international law

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why some scholars distinguish “society” from “state,” despite the terms sometimes being used loosely in everyday speech?
options: A society can exist without a formal government or defined political boundaries, whereas a state specifically requires a government, defined territory, and sovereignty
A society and a state are always identical, with no meaningful distinction
A state can exist without any population whatsoever
Society refers exclusively to economic relationships, with no cultural dimension
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: A society can exist without a formal government or defined political boundaries, whereas a state specifically requires a government, defined territory, and sovereignty

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains the significance of political culture in comparative government studies?
options: Political culture has no bearing on how political institutions actually function in practice
Political culture shapes how citizens perceive and interact with political institutions, helping to explain differences in how similar institutions function across different countries
Political culture is identical in every country, regardless of history or tradition
Political culture is relevant only to non- democratic states
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: Political culture shapes how citizens perceive and interact with political institutions, helping to explain differences in how similar institutions function across different countries

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a multi-ethnic state, such as many African countries, may face challenges in developing a strong sense of nationhood?
options: Multi-ethnic composition automatically guarantees national unity

Where multiple distinct ethnic or cultural groups exist within a single state’s borders, a shared overarching national identity may take considerable time and deliberate effort to develop, compared to a more culturally homogeneous state
Ethnic diversity has no bearing whatsoever on nation-building
A state can never achieve nationhood if it contains more than one ethnic group
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: Where multiple distinct ethnic or cultural groups exist within a single state’s borders, a shared overarching national identity may take considerable time and deliberate effort to develop, compared to a more culturally homogeneous state

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains the relationship between political participation and political socialization?
options: The two concepts are entirely unrelated
Political socialization often shapes the extent and manner of an individual’s later political participation, by instilling particular attitudes, values, and civic habits
Political participation always precedes political socialization in an individual’s life
Political socialization occurs only after an individual has already become politically active
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: Political socialization often shapes the extent and manner of an individual’s later political participation, by instilling particular attitudes, values, and civic habits

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why understanding basic political concepts such as power, authority, and legitimacy is important for analysing different systems of government?
options: These concepts have no practical application to real-world governance
These fundamental concepts provide the analytical tools needed to evaluate how governments acquire, exercise, and justify their rule, across differing political systems
These concepts apply only to democratic systems of government
Only legal scholars, and not political scientists, find these concepts useful
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: These fundamental concepts provide the analytical tools needed to evaluate how governments acquire, exercise, and justify their rule, across differing political systems

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a government reliant primarily on coercion, rather than legitimacy, is often considered less stable over the long term?
options: Coercive rule generally provokes no resistance whatsoever from the governed population
Reliance on force alone, without broader acceptance of the government’s right to rule, tends to generate resentment and resistance, making such regimes more vulnerable to instability or collapse
Coercion always guarantees indefinite political stability
Legitimacy has no bearing on a government’s long-term survival
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: Reliance on force alone, without broader acceptance of the government’s right to rule, tends to generate resentment and resistance, making such regimes more vulnerable to instability or collapse

Basic Concepts in Government.text: Which of the following correctly summarizes the overall importance of basic concepts such as power, authority, legitimacy, sovereignty, society, state, and nation in the study of government?
options: These concepts provide the essential conceptual vocabulary and analytical framework necessary for understanding how political systems are organized, function, and are justified
These basic concepts have no relevance beyond introductory academic study
Only historians, rather than political scientists, benefit from understanding these concepts
These concepts apply exclusively to Western political systems, with no relevance elsewhere
Basic Concepts in Government.correct_answer: These concepts provide the essential conceptual vocabulary and analytical framework necessary for understanding how political systems are organized, function, and are justified

Forms of Government.text: Monarchy is a form of government in which
options: supreme power rests with an elected assembly
supreme power is vested in a single ruler, typically inherited through a royal bloodline
power is shared equally among all citizens directly
power rests exclusively with a small group of wealthy elites
Forms of Government.correct_answer: supreme power is vested in a single ruler, typically inherited through a royal bloodline

Forms of Government.text: A constitutional monarchy differs from an absolute monarchy in that
options: the monarch’s powers are limited by a constitution, with real governing power often resting with an elected government
the monarch in a constitutional monarchy possesses unlimited powers
there is no meaningful difference between the two forms
a constitutional monarchy has no monarch at all
Forms of Government.correct_answer: the monarch’s powers are limited by a constitution, with real governing power often resting with an elected government

Forms of Government.text: Aristocracy is a form of government in which
options: power rests with the general population through direct voting
power rests with a privileged class, traditionally regarded as the “best” or most noble citizens
power rests with a single military dictator
power rests with the poorest members of society
Forms of Government.correct_answer: power rests with a privileged class, traditionally regarded as the “best” or most noble citizens

Forms of Government.text: Oligarchy is a form of government in which
options: power is exercised by a small, often self-interested group of people, such as the wealthy or a ruling elite
power is distributed equally among the entire citizenry
power rests solely with the judiciary
power is inherited by a single royal family
Forms of Government.correct_answer: power is exercised by a small, often self-interested group of people, such as the wealthy or a ruling elite

Forms of Government.text: Autocracy is a form of government in which
options: power is shared among multiple independent branches of government
supreme, unchecked power is concentrated in the hands of a single individual
power rests with an elected parliament
power is distributed among several competing political parties
Forms of Government.correct_answer: supreme, unchecked power is concentrated in the hands of a single individual

Forms of Government.text: Republicanism refers to a system of government in which
options: the head of state is a hereditary monarch
the head of state is typically an elected official, rather than a hereditary monarch, and government authority derives from the consent of the citizens
there is no head of state whatsoever
power is held exclusively by the military
Forms of Government.correct_answer: the head of state is typically an elected official, rather than a hereditary monarch, and government authority derives from the consent of the citizens

Forms of Government.text: Democracy, in its broadest sense, refers to a system of government in which
options: power is held by a single unelected ruler
political power ultimately derives from the people, typically exercised through free and fair elections and the protection of civil liberties
power is inherited through bloodline alone
only the wealthy are permitted to participate in governance
Forms of Government.correct_answer: political power ultimately derives from the people, typically exercised through free and fair elections and the protection of civil liberties

Forms of Government.text: A key merit commonly associated with monarchy, particularly a constitutional monarchy, is
options: the complete absence of any checks on the ruler’s power
continuity, stability, and a unifying symbol of national identity above partisan politics
that it eliminates the need for any elected government
that it guarantees economic prosperity automatically
Forms of Government.correct_answer: continuity, stability, and a unifying symbol of national identity above partisan politics

Forms of Government.text: A key demerit commonly associated with absolute monarchy is that
options: it distributes power too widely among the population
it concentrates power in a single hereditary ruler with little or no accountability, risking abuse of power
it requires frequent elections, which can be costly
it eliminates the role of tradition in governance
Forms of Government.correct_answer: it concentrates power in a single hereditary ruler with little or no accountability, risking abuse of power

Forms of Government.text: A key demerit commonly associated with oligarchy is that
options: it tends to serve the broad interests of the entire population equally
governance may serve the narrow interests of the ruling elite, rather than the wider public good
it guarantees equal representation for all citizens
it is identical in every respect to democracy
Forms of Government.correct_answer: governance may serve the narrow interests of the ruling elite, rather than the wider public good

Forms of Government.text: A key demerit commonly associated with autocracy is that
options: it distributes power widely, reducing the risk of abuse
the concentration of unchecked power in a single ruler increases the risk of tyranny and lack of accountability
it guarantees regular, free, and fair elections
it is identical in every respect to a constitutional monarchy
Forms of Government.correct_answer: the concentration of unchecked power in a single ruler increases the risk of tyranny and lack of accountability

Forms of Government.text: A key merit commonly associated with democracy is that
options: it concentrates all power in a single unelected leader
it allows for accountability, protection of civil liberties, and peaceful transfer of power through elections
it eliminates the need for a constitution
it guarantees that all policy decisions will always be correct
Forms of Government.correct_answer: it allows for accountability, protection of civil liberties, and peaceful transfer of power through elections

Forms of Government.text: A key demerit sometimes associated with democracy is that
options: it can be time-consuming, and may occasionally lead to short-term policy focus driven by electoral cycles
it always eliminates political disagreement entirely
it can never accommodate minority viewpoints
it inherently leads to permanent one-party rule
Forms of Government.correct_answer: it can be time-consuming, and may occasionally lead to short-term policy focus driven by electoral cycles

Forms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes aristocracy from oligarchy?
options: Aristocracy is based on a claim to inherited nobility or perceived merit, while oligarchy is based more broadly on the concentration of power in a small group, often defined by wealth or influence, without necessarily any claim to noble birth
The two terms are entirely identical, with no meaningful distinction
Oligarchy always involves inherited nobility, while aristocracy never does
Aristocracy always involves elections, while oligarchy never does
Forms of Government.correct_answer: Aristocracy is based on a claim to inherited nobility or perceived merit, while oligarchy is based more broadly on the concentration of power in a small group, often defined by wealth or influence, without necessarily any claim to noble birth

Forms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a constitutional monarchy, such as that of the United Kingdom, is often considered compatible with democratic governance?
options: The monarch typically retains largely ceremonial functions, while actual governing power rests with an elected parliament and government accountable to the people
The monarch in such a system holds absolute, unchecked power over all government decisions
Constitutional monarchies never hold elections of any kind
A constitutional monarchy is identical in every respect to an absolute monarchy
Forms of Government.correct_answer: The monarch typically retains largely ceremonial functions, while actual governing power rests with an elected parliament and government accountable to the people

Forms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why autocracy is often considered particularly vulnerable to poor governance decisions?
options: The concentration of decision-making in a single individual removes meaningful checks and balances that might otherwise catch and correct flawed or self-serving policies
Autocracies always produce superior governance outcomes compared to other systems
Autocratic rulers are legally required to consult the citizenry before making decisions
Checks and balances have no relevance to the quality of governance under any system
Forms of Government.correct_answer: The concentration of decision-making in a single individual removes meaningful checks and balances that might otherwise catch and correct flawed or self-serving policies

Forms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains a key practical distinction between a republic and a monarchy?
options: A republic’s head of state is typically elected or otherwise selected through a non- hereditary process, whereas a monarchy’s head of state typically inherits the position through a royal bloodline
A republic always has a hereditary head of state, similarly to a monarchy
There is no meaningful practical distinction between the two systems
Monarchies never have any form of elected government whatsoever
Forms of Government.correct_answer: A republic’s head of state is typically elected or otherwise selected through a non- hereditary process, whereas a monarchy’s head of state typically inherits the position through a royal bloodline

Forms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why democracy is generally regarded as more accountable than autocracy?
options: Regular elections and independent institutions in a democracy allow citizens to remove leaders who perform poorly or abuse power, a mechanism generally absent or weak under autocratic rule
Autocracies generally provide more frequent and effective accountability mechanisms than democracies
Accountability is irrelevant to the classification of forms of government
Democracies never hold their leaders accountable in any meaningful way
Forms of Government.correct_answer: Regular elections and independent institutions in a democracy allow citizens to remove leaders who perform poorly or abuse power, a mechanism generally absent or weak under autocratic rule

Forms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why oligarchic rule can sometimes emerge even within nominally democratic systems?
options: Wealthy or influential groups may disproportionately shape political outcomes through their access to resources, media, or political connections, even where formal democratic institutions and elections exist
Oligarchy and democracy are entirely mutually exclusive, and could never coexist in any form
Wealth and influence have no bearing whatsoever on political outcomes in any system
Formal democratic institutions automatically prevent any disproportionate influence by elite groups
Forms of Government.correct_answer: Wealthy or influential groups may disproportionately shape political outcomes through their access to resources, media, or political connections, even where formal democratic institutions and elections exist

Forms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why republicanism is often closely associated with, though not strictly identical to, democracy?
options: Most modern republics are also democracies, since they typically feature elected leadership and popular sovereignty, though a republic could theoretically exist without full democratic practices
Republicanism and democracy are, in fact, entirely unrelated concepts
Every republic in history has always been fully democratic, with no exceptions whatsoever
A monarchy is a specific type of republic
Forms of Government.correct_answer: Most modern republics are also democracies, since they typically feature elected leadership and popular sovereignty, though a republic could theoretically exist without full democratic practices

Forms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why direct democracy, in which citizens vote directly on most policy issues, is relatively rare in large modern states?
options: Practical challenges of scale, time, and complexity generally make it more feasible for large states to adopt representative democracy, in which citizens elect representatives to make decisions on their behalf
Direct democracy is, in fact, the most common form of governance in large modern states
Large states generally find direct democracy easier to implement than representative democracy
Scale and complexity have no bearing on the practicality of direct democracy
Forms of Government.correct_answer: Practical challenges of scale, time, and complexity generally make it more feasible for large states to adopt representative democracy, in which citizens elect representatives to make decisions on their behalf

Forms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why autocratic regimes often restrict press freedom and political opposition?
options: Limiting independent scrutiny and organized opposition helps an autocratic ruler maintain unchecked power, by reducing the ability of citizens to challenge or remove the regime
Autocratic regimes generally promote a free press and vibrant political opposition, in order to strengthen their own rule
Press freedom and political opposition have no bearing on an autocratic ruler’s ability to maintain power
All forms of government, regardless of type, restrict press freedom to an identical degree
Forms of Government.correct_answer: Limiting independent scrutiny and organized opposition helps an autocratic ruler maintain unchecked power, by reducing the ability of citizens to challenge or remove the regime

Forms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why some historical monarchies gradually evolved into constitutional monarchies over time?
options: Growing demands from citizens and emerging political classes for greater representation and accountability often led to negotiated or forced limitations on the monarch’s formerly absolute powers
Monarchs generally voluntarily surrendered all of their power with no external pressure whatsoever
Constitutional monarchies emerged entirely independently of any historical demand for greater political representation
Absolute monarchy and constitutional monarchy have always existed as entirely separate, unrelated systems, with no historical evolution between them
Forms of Government.correct_answer: Growing demands from citizens and emerging political classes for greater representation and accountability often led to negotiated or forced limitations on the monarch’s formerly absolute powers

Forms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a small group exercising oligarchic control might resist democratic reforms?
options: Democratic reforms, such as broader suffrage or free elections, could threaten the disproportionate power and privileges the oligarchic group currently enjoys
Oligarchic groups typically welcome democratic reforms that would reduce their own influence
Democratic reforms have no bearing on the interests of an entrenched oligarchic elite
Oligarchy and democratic reform are always perfectly compatible, with no inherent tension
Forms of Government.correct_answer: Democratic reforms, such as broader suffrage or free elections, could threaten the disproportionate power and privileges the oligarchic group currently enjoys

Forms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why classifying a real-world government strictly into a single “pure” form (such as pure democracy or pure autocracy) can sometimes be an oversimplification?
options: Many actual governments exhibit a blend of characteristics from different forms of government, making rigid classification into a single pure category potentially misleading
Every real-world government fits perfectly and exclusively into one single, pure category, with no overlap whatsoever
Classification of governments into different forms serves no useful analytical purpose whatsoever
All forms of government are, in practice, functionally identical to one another
Forms of Government.correct_answer: Many actual governments exhibit a blend of characteristics from different forms of government, making rigid classification into a single pure category potentially misleading

Forms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why some political theorists view aristocracy, in its original conception, as intending to place governance in the hands of the most capable or virtuous members of society?
options: The term aristocracy derives from a claim that rule by a select, supposedly superior class would produce better governance outcomes than rule by the broader population
Aristocracy was originally conceived specifically to ensure equal representation of all social classes
The concept of aristocracy has no historical connection to claims of merit or virtue
Aristocracy and democracy share an identical underlying philosophical justification
Forms of Government.correct_answer: The term aristocracy derives from a claim that rule by a select, supposedly superior class would produce better governance outcomes than rule by the broader population

Forms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why hybrid or mixed systems of government, combining elements of different forms, have historically been proposed by political philosophers?
options: Mixed systems, such as those combining monarchical, aristocratic, and democratic elements, were sometimes proposed as a way to balance the perceived strengths and weaknesses of any single pure form of government
Political philosophers have historically always insisted that only pure, unmixed forms of government could ever function effectively
Mixed systems of government have no historical basis in political theory whatsoever
Combining different forms of government always results in a system identical to pure autocracy
Forms of Government.correct_answer: Mixed systems, such as those combining monarchical, aristocratic, and democratic elements, were sometimes proposed as a way to balance the perceived strengths and weaknesses of any single pure form of government

Forms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why some modern states retain a ceremonial monarch alongside fully democratic institutions?
options: A ceremonial monarch can provide a unifying symbol of national continuity and tradition, while day-to-day governance and policy-making remain firmly in the hands of elected, accountable institutions
A ceremonial monarch in such systems typically retains full, unchecked governing power
The presence of a ceremonial monarch is entirely incompatible with any form of democratic governance
Ceremonial monarchies serve no meaningful social or political function whatsoever
Forms of Government.correct_answer: A ceremonial monarch can provide a unifying symbol of national continuity and tradition, while day-to-day governance and policy-making remain firmly in the hands of elected, accountable institutions

Forms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the specific merits and demerits of a given form of government (such as monarchy, oligarchy, or democracy) can vary considerably, depending on how that particular system is actually implemented in practice?
options: The formal classification of a government’s type does not fully determine outcomes; factors such as the strength of institutions, rule of law, and actual accountability mechanisms significantly shape real-world governance quality within any given form
Every government sharing the same formal classification will, without exception, produce identical governance outcomes
The manner of implementation has no bearing whatsoever on the practical merits or demerits of a given form of government
Only democracies can, in principle, ever be implemented well or poorly; all other forms are always implemented identically
Forms of Government.correct_answer: The formal classification of a government’s type does not fully determine outcomes; factors such as the strength of institutions, rule of law, and actual accountability mechanisms significantly shape real-world governance quality within any given form

Forms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly summarizes the overall importance of studying differing forms of government, such as monarchy, aristocracy, oligarchy, autocracy, republicanism, and democracy?
options: Understanding these differing forms provides a comparative framework for analysing how political power is acquired, distributed, and exercised across different societies and historical periods
Studying different forms of government has no practical or academic value whatsoever
Only democracy is worthy of serious academic study; all other forms are irrelevant
Forms of government have remained entirely static throughout history, with no meaningful variation or evolution
Forms of Government.correct_answer: Understanding these differing forms provides a comparative framework for analysing how political power is acquired, distributed, and exercised across different societies and historical periods

Arms of Government.text: The legislature is the arm of government primarily responsible for
options: enforcing and implementing laws
making, amending, and repealing laws
interpreting laws and adjudicating disputes
commanding the armed forces
Arms of Government.correct_answer: making, amending, and repealing laws

Arms of Government.text: A unicameral legislature is one that
options: consists of two separate chambers or houses
consists of a single chamber or house
has no elected members whatsoever
exists only in monarchies
Arms of Government.correct_answer: consists of a single chamber or house

Arms of Government.text: A bicameral legislature is one that
options: consists of a single chamber or house
consists of two separate chambers or houses, typically an upper and a lower house
has no elected members whatsoever
exists only in unitary states
Arms of Government.correct_answer: consists of two separate chambers or houses, typically an upper and a lower house

Arms of Government.text: In Nigeria’s National Assembly, the two chambers are known as
options: the House of Lords and the House of Commons
the Senate and the House of Representatives
the Upper Chamber and the Federal Chamber
the Congress and the Parliament
Arms of Government.correct_answer: the Senate and the House of Representatives

Arms of Government.text: A key function of the legislature includes
options: enforcing court judgments directly
law-making, representation of constituents, and oversight of the executive
commanding military operations
appointing all civil servants directly
Arms of Government.correct_answer: law-making, representation of constituents, and oversight of the executive

Arms of Government.text: The executive is the arm of government primarily responsible for
options: making laws
implementing and enforcing laws and public policy
interpreting laws in court
representing constituents in the legislature
Arms of Government.correct_answer: implementing and enforcing laws and public policy

Arms of Government.text: In a presidential system, the executive is typically
options: headed by a prime minister who is also a member of the legislature
headed by a president who is elected separately from the legislature, and who serves as both head of state and head of government
entirely appointed by the judiciary
composed exclusively of unelected civil servants
Arms of Government.correct_answer: headed by a president who is elected separately from the legislature, and who serves as both head of state and head of government

Arms of Government.text: In a parliamentary system, the executive (typically the prime minister and cabinet) is generally
options: elected entirely separately from the legislature
drawn from, and accountable to, the legislature (parliament)
appointed solely by the judiciary
composed entirely of military officers
Arms of Government.correct_answer: drawn from, and accountable to, the legislature (parliament)

Arms of Government.text: The judiciary is the arm of government primarily responsible for
options: making laws
interpreting and applying laws, and adjudicating legal disputes
implementing government policy and administration
representing citizens in elections
Arms of Government.correct_answer: interpreting and applying laws, and adjudicating legal disputes

Arms of Government.text: Judicial independence refers to
options: the judiciary’s freedom from undue influence or control by the executive or legislature, allowing impartial adjudication
the judiciary’s complete lack of any legal authority whatsoever
a situation in which judges are directly elected by popular vote in every country
the judiciary’s subordination to the executive arm of government
Arms of Government.correct_answer: the judiciary’s freedom from undue influence or control by the executive or legislature, allowing impartial adjudication

Arms of Government.text: Judicial review refers to the power of courts to
options: draft new legislation directly
examine and determine whether laws or executive actions are consistent with the constitution
command the armed forces
appoint members of the legislature
Arms of Government.correct_answer: examine and determine whether laws or executive actions are consistent with the constitution

Arms of Government.text: The power of the legislature to scrutinize and check the actions of the executive is generally known as
options: judicial review
legislative oversight
executive privilege
constitutional amendment
Arms of Government.correct_answer: legislative oversight

Arms of Government.text: In Nigeria’s National Assembly, the Senate is generally regarded as
options: the lower chamber
the upper chamber
an advisory body with no formal legislative powers
a purely ceremonial body
Arms of Government.correct_answer: the upper chamber

Arms of Government.text: In Nigeria’s National Assembly, the House of Representatives is generally regarded as
options: the upper chamber
the lower chamber
a purely advisory body with no legislative powers
a body composed exclusively of traditional rulers
Arms of Government.correct_answer: the lower chamber

Arms of Government.text: A bill becomes law in most legislative systems only after it has
options: been drafted by a single legislator, with no further process required
passed through the required legislative stages (such as readings and committee review) and received the required assent, often from the head of state or executive
been approved solely by the judiciary
been announced publicly, with no formal legislative process required
Arms of Government.correct_answer: passed through the required legislative stages (such as readings and committee review) and received the required assent, often from the head of state or executive

Arms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the separation of the legislature, executive, and judiciary into distinct arms of government is generally considered important?
options: It concentrates all governmental power in a single arm, for efficiency
It helps prevent the excessive concentration of power in any single arm, promoting checks and balances and reducing the risk of tyranny
It has no meaningful effect on how power is exercised within a government
It applies only to authoritarian systems of government
Arms of Government.correct_answer: It helps prevent the excessive concentration of power in any single arm, promoting checks and balances and reducing the risk of tyranny

Arms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains the relationship between the legislature and the executive under a presidential system, such as that of Nigeria and the United States?
options: The executive and legislature are elected separately and function with a significant degree of independence from one another, subject to checks and balances
The executive is always drawn entirely from, and directly accountable to, the legislature
There is, in practice, no meaningful distinction between the legislature and the executive in a presidential system
The legislature has no oversight role whatsoever over the executive in a presidential system
Arms of Government.correct_answer: The executive and legislature are elected separately and function with a significant degree of independence from one another, subject to checks and balances

Arms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains a key functional difference between a parliamentary and a presidential system, regarding the relationship between the executive and legislature?
options: In a parliamentary system, the executive is typically drawn from and remains accountable to the legislature, whereas in a presidential system, the executive is elected separately and enjoys a fixed term independent of ongoing legislative confidence
There is no meaningful functional difference between the two systems in this respect
In a presidential system, the executive is always drawn directly from the legislature
In a parliamentary system, the executive is always elected entirely independently of the legislature
Arms of Government.correct_answer: In a parliamentary system, the executive is typically drawn from and remains accountable to the legislature, whereas in a presidential system, the executive is elected separately and enjoys a fixed term independent of ongoing legislative confidence

Arms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains the significance of judicial independence for the proper functioning of a democratic system of government?
options: Judicial independence has no meaningful bearing on democratic governance

An independent judiciary can impartially adjudicate disputes, including those involving the government itself, helping to uphold the rule of law and protect citizens’ rights against potential abuses of power
Judicial independence is only relevant in non-democratic systems
A judiciary that is fully controlled by the executive is generally considered ideal for democratic governance
Arms of Government.correct_answer: An independent judiciary can impartially adjudicate disputes, including those involving the government itself, helping to uphold the rule of law and protect citizens’ rights against potential abuses of power

Arms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why judicial review is considered an important check on the other arms of government?
options: It allows the judiciary to strike down or invalidate laws or executive actions found to be inconsistent with the constitution, thereby helping to ensure that neither the legislature nor the executive exceeds its constitutional authority
Judicial review grants the judiciary unlimited power to create new legislation
Judicial review has no meaningful effect on the actions of the legislature or executive
Judicial review is a power exercised exclusively by the legislature, not the judiciary
Arms of Government.correct_answer: It allows the judiciary to strike down or invalidate laws or executive actions found to be inconsistent with the constitution, thereby helping to ensure that neither the legislature nor the executive exceeds its constitutional authority

Arms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why legislative oversight of the executive is considered an important democratic function?
options: It allows the legislature to monitor, question, and hold the executive accountable for its policies, spending, and administration, helping to prevent abuse of power
Legislative oversight has no meaningful bearing on executive accountability
Legislative oversight is a power exercised exclusively by the judiciary
The executive is entirely exempt from any legislative scrutiny under all systems of government
Arms of Government.correct_answer: It allows the legislature to monitor, question, and hold the executive accountable for its policies, spending, and administration, helping to prevent abuse of power

Arms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains a key advantage commonly associated with a bicameral legislature, compared to a unicameral one?
options: A bicameral legislature eliminates the need for any legislative process whatsoever
A bicameral legislature can provide an additional layer of scrutiny and deliberation, as legislation typically must pass through two separate chambers before becoming law
A bicameral legislature always makes the law-making process faster than a unicameral legislature
A bicameral legislature has no meaningful advantage over a unicameral legislature
Arms of Government.correct_answer: A bicameral legislature can provide an additional layer of scrutiny and deliberation, as legislation typically must pass through two separate chambers before becoming law

Arms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains a potential disadvantage sometimes associated with a bicameral legislature?
options: The requirement for legislation to pass through two chambers can potentially slow down the law-making process, compared to a unicameral system
A bicameral legislature always guarantees faster passage of legislation than a unicameral system
Bicameral legislatures have no meaningful disadvantages whatsoever
A bicameral legislature eliminates the possibility of legislative disagreement
Arms of Government.correct_answer: The requirement for legislation to pass through two chambers can potentially slow down the law-making process, compared to a unicameral system

Arms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the executive arm of government is generally responsible for the day-to-day administration of public policy, rather than the legislature?
options: The executive typically possesses the administrative machinery, including ministries and agencies, needed to implement and enforce the laws and policies enacted by the legislature
The legislature is generally better equipped than the executive to handle day-to-day administrative implementation
The executive has no meaningful role in implementing legislation once it is passed
Administrative implementation is generally handled exclusively by the judiciary
Arms of Government.correct_answer: The executive typically possesses the administrative machinery, including ministries and agencies, needed to implement and enforce the laws and policies enacted by the legislature

Arms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why courts, as part of the judiciary, are generally expected to interpret laws rather than create new legislation?
options: Interpreting and applying existing law, rather than creating new law, is generally considered the proper constitutional role of the judiciary, with law-making reserved for the legislature, in keeping with the separation of powers
Courts are generally expected to create entirely new legislation whenever they consider existing law to be inadequate
The judiciary and legislature are generally understood to share an identical constitutional function
The separation of powers has no bearing on the proper role of the judiciary
Arms of Government.correct_answer: Interpreting and applying existing law, rather than creating new law, is generally considered the proper constitutional role of the judiciary, with law-making reserved for the legislature, in keeping with the separation of powers

Arms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the relationship between the legislature and the executive can sometimes lead to political gridlock, particularly under a presidential system with divided government (where different parties control the legislature and executive)?
options: Since the executive and legislature are elected separately and may be controlled by rival political parties, disagreements between the two arms can sometimes delay or block the passage of legislation or policy initiatives
Divided government under a presidential system always results in perfectly smooth, unanimous cooperation between the legislature and executive
Political gridlock can, in principle, only ever occur under a parliamentary system, never under a presidential system
The composition of the legislature and executive has no bearing whatsoever on the likelihood of political gridlock
Arms of Government.correct_answer: Since the executive and legislature are elected separately and may be controlled by rival political parties, disagreements between the two arms can sometimes delay or block the passage of legislation or policy initiatives

Arms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why representation is considered a core function of the legislature, distinct from its law-making role?
options: Legislators, particularly in a representative democracy, are generally expected to voice and advocate for the interests, concerns, and preferences of their particular constituents, in addition to their broader law-making responsibilities
Representation is a function generally associated exclusively with the judiciary, rather than the legislature
Legislators generally have no meaningful obligation to represent the interests of their constituents
Representation and law-making are, in practice, entirely identical legislative functions with no meaningful distinction
Arms of Government.correct_answer: Legislators, particularly in a representative democracy, are generally expected to voice and advocate for the interests, concerns, and preferences of their particular constituents, in addition to their broader law-making responsibilities

Arms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the head of state and head of government are combined in a single office (such as the President) under many presidential systems, unlike in many parliamentary systems where these roles are often separated?
options: A presidential system’s constitutional design generally consolidates both ceremonial (head of state) and executive/governing (head of government) functions within a single elected office, whereas parliamentary systems often separate these roles between a largely ceremonial head of state (such as a monarch or president) and a governing head of government (such as a prime minister)
Presidential systems generally always maintain entirely separate individuals for the head of state and head of government roles
Parliamentary systems generally never separate the head of state and head of government roles
The distinction between head of state and head of government has no meaningful relevance to the classification of presidential versus parliamentary systems
Arms of Government.correct_answer: A presidential system’s constitutional design generally consolidates both ceremonial (head of state) and executive/governing (head of government) functions within a single elected office, whereas parliamentary systems often separate these roles between a largely ceremonial head of state (such as a monarch or president) and a governing head of government (such as a prime minister)

Arms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the specific procedural stages a bill must pass through in the legislature (such as multiple readings and committee review) are considered important safeguards in the law-making process?
options: These procedural stages generally provide opportunities for detailed scrutiny, debate, and amendment of proposed legislation, helping to improve the overall quality of laws and reduce the likelihood of hastily passed, poorly considered legislation
Procedural stages in the legislative process generally serve no meaningful safeguarding function whatsoever
A bill can generally become law immediately upon being drafted, with no further procedural requirement
Detailed scrutiny and debate have no bearing on the overall quality of resulting legislation
Arms of Government.correct_answer: These procedural stages generally provide opportunities for detailed scrutiny, debate, and amendment of proposed legislation, helping to improve the overall quality of laws and reduce the likelihood of hastily passed, poorly considered legislation

Arms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the relationship between the three arms of government is often described using the concept of “checks and balances,” rather than simply “separation of powers” alone?
options: Beyond merely dividing governmental functions among distinct arms, each arm is typically also granted specific powers to monitor, restrain, or check the actions of the other arms, helping to prevent the abuse of power by any single arm
Checks and balances and separation of powers are, in practice, entirely identical concepts, with no meaningful distinction between them
Under a proper system of separation of powers, no arm of government generally has any power whatsoever to check or restrain any other arm
The concept of checks and balances generally applies only to non-democratic systems of government
Arms of Government.correct_answer: Beyond merely dividing governmental functions among distinct arms, each arm is typically also granted specific powers to monitor, restrain, or check the actions of the other arms, helping to prevent the abuse of power by any single arm

Arms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why an independent judiciary is often considered particularly important for protecting minority rights within a democratic society?
options: An independent judiciary can, in principle, rule against majoritarian legislative or executive actions that violate constitutionally protected minority rights, providing a check against potential majority overreach
An independent judiciary generally has no meaningful role in protecting the rights of minority groups
Judicial independence is generally relevant only to disputes between private individuals, with no bearing on constitutional rights
Minority rights are, in practice, always adequately protected by the legislature alone, with no need for judicial involvement
Arms of Government.correct_answer: An independent judiciary can, in principle, rule against majoritarian legislative or executive actions that violate constitutionally protected minority rights, providing a check against potential majority overreach

Arms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the executive’s power to veto legislation, found in some presidential systems, is generally considered an important check on the legislature?
options: A veto power generally allows the executive to reject legislation it considers flawed or objectionable, though this power is often itself subject to a further check, such as legislative override with a sufficient majority
An executive veto generally grants the executive unlimited, unchecked power to permanently block any legislation
The power to veto legislation is generally exercised exclusively by the judiciary, rather than the executive
Executive veto power has no meaningful role within a system of checks and balances
Arms of Government.correct_answer: A veto power generally allows the executive to reject legislation it considers flawed or objectionable, though this power is often itself subject to a further check, such as legislative override with a sufficient majority

Arms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the specific structure and powers of the legislature, executive, and judiciary can vary meaningfully between different countries, despite sharing the same general threefold classification?
options: Constitutional design choices, historical development, and particular political circumstances generally shape how each country structures and allocates power among its three arms of government, resulting in meaningful variation despite a shared general framework
Every country in the world generally structures its three arms of government in an entirely identical manner
The general classification into legislature, executive, and judiciary generally allows for no meaningful variation whatsoever between different countries
Constitutional design and historical development generally have no bearing on how a country structures its arms of government
Arms of Government.correct_answer: Constitutional design choices, historical development, and particular political circumstances generally shape how each country structures and allocates power among its three arms of government, resulting in meaningful variation despite a shared general framework

Arms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why effective interrelationship and cooperation among the three arms of government, despite their formal separation, is generally considered necessary for a government to function effectively?
options: While the arms of government are formally separated to prevent excessive concentration of power, practical governance generally still requires a meaningful degree of coordination and cooperation among them, such as the executive implementing laws passed by the legislature, and the judiciary relying on the executive to enforce its judgments
The three arms of government are generally expected to operate in complete isolation from one another, with absolutely no interaction or cooperation whatsoever
Effective governance generally requires that one single arm of government exercise complete, unchecked control over the other two arms
Coordination among the three arms of government has no meaningful bearing on overall government effectiveness
Arms of Government.correct_answer: While the arms of government are formally separated to prevent excessive concentration of power, practical governance generally still requires a meaningful degree of coordination and cooperation among them, such as the executive implementing laws passed by the legislature, and the judiciary relying on the executive to enforce its judgments

Arms of Government.text: Which of the following correctly summarizes the overall importance of understanding the legislature, executive, and judiciary as distinct arms of government, along with their interrelationships?
options: A clear understanding of the distinct roles, powers, and interrelationships of these three arms is fundamental to analysing how political power is organized, exercised, and checked within any given system of government
The distinction between the legislature, executive, and judiciary has no meaningful analytical value in the study of government
Only the executive arm is genuinely significant for understanding how a government actually functions
The three arms of government are, in practice, functionally identical to one another, with no meaningful distinction
Arms of Government.correct_answer: A clear understanding of the distinct roles, powers, and interrelationships of these three arms is fundamental to analysing how political power is organized, exercised, and checked within any given system of government

Structures of Governance.text: A unitary system of government is one in which
options: governing power is constitutionally divided between a central government and several constituent regional governments
supreme governing power is concentrated in a single central government, which may delegate limited authority to local units
two or more independent states voluntarily join together, each retaining significant sovereignty
power is exercised jointly by a monarch and an elected parliament
Structures of Governance.correct_answer: supreme governing power is concentrated in a single central government, which may delegate limited authority to local units

Structures of Governance.text: A federal system of government is one in which
options: all governing power rests solely with a single central authority
governing power is constitutionally divided between a central (federal) government and constituent states or regions, each with its own defined sphere of authority
constituent states retain the right to secede at any time, with the central government having no binding authority
there is no central government whatsoever
Structures of Governance.correct_answer: governing power is constitutionally divided between a central (federal) government and constituent states or regions, each with its own defined sphere of authority

Structures of Governance.text: A confederal system of government is one in which
options: a strong central government holds all effective power over constituent units
independent states voluntarily form a loose association for specific common purposes, while each retaining significant sovereignty and the right to withdraw
power is concentrated entirely in a single hereditary monarch
local governments possess no constitutional recognition whatsoever
Structures of Governance.correct_answer: independent states voluntarily form a loose association for specific common purposes, while each retaining significant sovereignty and the right to withdraw

Structures of Governance.text: A key feature of a unitary system is that
options: local or regional governments possess constitutionally guaranteed, independent powers that the central government cannot unilaterally alter
local or regional governments derive their powers from the central government, which may create, alter, or abolish them
there is no central government of any kind
each region has its own separate military force
Structures of Governance.correct_answer: local or regional governments derive their powers from the central government, which may create, alter, or abolish them

Structures of Governance.text: A key feature of a federal system is that
options: the powers of the constituent states are typically entrenched in a constitution and cannot be unilaterally altered by the central government alone
all governmental power is concentrated exclusively in the central government
constituent states have no defined territory
there is no written constitution in any federal system
Structures of Governance.correct_answer: the powers of the constituent states are typically entrenched in a constitution and cannot be unilaterally altered by the central government alone

Structures of Governance.text: A commonly cited reason for adopting a unitary system of government is
options: the desire to accommodate significant ethnic, cultural, or regional diversity through devolved regional autonomy
the desire for administrative uniformity, efficiency, and strong national cohesion, particularly in relatively small or culturally homogeneous states
the desire to allow constituent regions the right to secede freely
the complete absence of any need for central coordination
Structures of Governance.correct_answer: the desire for administrative uniformity, efficiency, and strong national cohesion, particularly in relatively small or culturally homogeneous states

Structures of Governance.text: A commonly cited reason for adopting a federal system of government is
options: the desire for complete administrative uniformity across all regions
the need to accommodate significant diversity (ethnic, religious, or regional) within a large or heterogeneous country, by granting constituent units a degree of self-governance
the desire to eliminate all forms of local government
the complete absence of any need for a central government
Structures of Governance.correct_answer: the need to accommodate significant diversity (ethnic, religious, or regional) within a large or heterogeneous country, by granting constituent units a degree of self-governance

Structures of Governance.text: A commonly cited merit of a unitary system is
options: administrative simplicity and the ability to implement uniform policies nationwide relatively easily
the guarantee of complete regional independence for all constituent units
the complete absence of any central authority
the automatic elimination of any risk of ethnic tension
Structures of Governance.correct_answer: administrative simplicity and the ability to implement uniform policies nationwide relatively easily

Structures of Governance.text: A commonly cited demerit of a unitary system, particularly in a large or diverse country, is that
options: it always guarantees perfect representation of all regional interests
excessive centralization may fail to adequately address the specific needs and interests of diverse regions, potentially fuelling resentment or agitation
it eliminates the possibility of any central government policy whatsoever
it grants constituent regions unlimited sovereign power
Structures of Governance.correct_answer: excessive centralization may fail to adequately address the specific needs and interests of diverse regions, potentially fuelling resentment or agitation

Structures of Governance.text: A commonly cited merit of a federal system is that
options: it can accommodate regional diversity while maintaining national unity, allowing constituent units some autonomy over local matters
it always results in weaker national defence than a unitary system
it eliminates the need for any central government
it guarantees that no disputes will ever arise between the central and state governments
Structures of Governance.correct_answer: it can accommodate regional diversity while maintaining national unity, allowing constituent units some autonomy over local matters

Structures of Governance.text: A commonly cited demerit of a federal system is that
options: it always eliminates regional diversity entirely
it can lead to duplication of institutions, higher administrative costs, and potential conflicts over the division of powers between the central and state governments
it grants the central government unlimited power over the constituent states
it prevents the existence of any local government whatsoever
Structures of Governance.correct_answer: it can lead to duplication of institutions, higher administrative costs, and potential conflicts over the division of powers between the central and state governments

Structures of Governance.text: A commonly cited reason for adopting a confederal system is
options: the desire for a single, unified central government with complete control over all member states
the desire of independent, sovereign states to cooperate on specific shared interests (such as defence or trade) while retaining maximum individual sovereignty
the complete elimination of national sovereignty for all member states
the establishment of a single, indivisible nation-state
Structures of Governance.correct_answer: the desire of independent, sovereign states to cooperate on specific shared interests (such as defence or trade) while retaining maximum individual sovereignty

Structures of Governance.text: A commonly cited merit of a confederal system is that
options: it allows independent states to cooperate on matters of mutual interest while preserving a high degree of individual sovereignty and autonomy
it always results in a single, unified central government with unlimited authority
it eliminates the need for cooperation between member states entirely
it guarantees permanent, irrevocable political union among member states
Structures of Governance.correct_answer: it allows independent states to cooperate on matters of mutual interest while preserving a high degree of individual sovereignty and autonomy

Structures of Governance.text: A commonly cited demerit of a confederal system is that
options: the loose, voluntary nature of the association can result in weak central coordination and difficulty enforcing collective decisions on member states
it always guarantees strong, effective central enforcement of all decisions
member states have no ability whatsoever to withdraw from the confederation
it eliminates all forms of state sovereignty
Structures of Governance.correct_answer: the loose, voluntary nature of the association can result in weak central coordination and difficulty enforcing collective decisions on member states

Structures of Governance.text: Which of the following correctly explains why Nigeria adopted a federal system of government, rather than a unitary system, following independence?
options: Nigeria’s significant ethnic, religious, and regional diversity was considered better accommodated through a federal structure granting some autonomy to constituent states, compared to a more centralized unitary system
Nigeria’s relative ethnic and regional homogeneity made a federal system entirely unnecessary
Federal systems are, in principle, only suitable for very small, culturally uniform countries
The choice between unitary and federal systems has no bearing on how a country’s diversity is managed
Structures of Governance.correct_answer: Nigeria’s significant ethnic, religious, and regional diversity was considered better accommodated through a federal structure granting some autonomy to constituent states, compared to a more centralized unitary system

Structures of Governance.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the European Union is often cited as an example exhibiting some confederal characteristics, despite also possessing certain features associated with a more integrated union?
options: Member states of the European Union retain considerable sovereignty, including the right to withdraw (as demonstrated by Brexit), while cooperating closely on shared policy areas, reflecting some characteristics generally associated with confederal arrangements
The European Union functions as a single, fully unitary state, with no meaningful sovereignty retained by individual member states
Confederal characteristics are entirely absent from the structure of the European Union
Member states of the European Union have no ability whatsoever to withdraw from the union
Structures of Governance.correct_answer: Member states of the European Union retain considerable sovereignty, including the right to withdraw (as demonstrated by Brexit), while cooperating closely on shared policy areas, reflecting some characteristics generally associated with confederal arrangements

Structures of Governance.text: Which of the following correctly explains why small island nations, such as Singapore, often adopt a unitary rather than federal system of government?
options: Their relatively small size and often more culturally homogeneous population may make the administrative complexity of a federal system unnecessary, favouring the simplicity and efficiency of a unitary structure
Small island nations generally always require the accommodation of extensive regional diversity through a federal structure
Size and cultural homogeneity generally have no bearing on the choice between unitary and federal systems
Federal systems are, in principle, always simpler to administer than unitary systems
Structures of Governance.correct_answer: Their relatively small size and often more culturally homogeneous population may make the administrative complexity of a federal system unnecessary, favouring the simplicity and efficiency of a unitary structure

Structures of Governance.text: Which of the following correctly explains why disputes over the division of powers between central and state governments are a common feature of federal systems?
options: Since federal constitutions typically attempt to precisely delineate which matters fall under central versus state jurisdiction, ambiguities or overlapping areas of authority can generate ongoing disputes requiring judicial or political resolution
Federal constitutions generally eliminate any possibility of disputes over the division of powers
Disputes over the division of powers are, in principle, unique to unitary systems, never occurring under a federal system
The division of powers between central and state governments has no bearing on the likelihood of intergovernmental disputes
Structures of Governance.correct_answer: Since federal constitutions typically attempt to precisely delineate which matters fall under central versus state jurisdiction, ambiguities or overlapping areas of authority can generate ongoing disputes requiring judicial or political resolution

Structures of Governance.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a confederation is generally considered a looser, less permanent form of political association compared to a federation?
